blocks.value: A control structure directs the flow of a program away from simple top-to-bottom execution. There are two kinds: a selection structure picks which statements run based on a condition, and a repetition structure repeats statements based on a condition.
The simplest selection is a one-way if. It runs a block only when its condition is true, and does nothing otherwise:
A two-way selection uses if...else. The else block runs whenever the if condition is false:
Any group of statements wrapped in { }, like the body of an if block, is called a compound statement (or block). It can contain as many statements as needed, all executed together.
